newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Letter bomb explodes in Austria, no one hurt.
newsitem.headline: Letter bomb explodes in Austria, no one hurt.

text.p: A letter bomb sent to an unidentified 50-year-old woman exploded in a working-class district of Vienna on Monday but no one was injured in the blast, the Interior Ministry said.
The woman became suspicious of a package and informed police who took the device away just before it exploded, a ministry spokeswoman said.
A bomb disposal expert was called to the scene in the district of Favoriten in the east of the city to deal with the device, police said.
No group has yet claimed responsibility for sending the device, but the so-called Bajuwarian Liberation Army (BLA) has admitted sending more than a score of letter bombs in the past three years.

Police have also linked the group to the murder of four gypsy men in February last year, who died instantly when they tried to remove a racist sign reading "Roma (gypsies) back to India", setting off a booby-trapped bomb.
Five series of letter bombs sent since 1993 have been aimed at foreigners or figures linked to refugee or immigration issues. Twelve people have been injured in the explosions.
One blast ripped off three fingers of former Vienna mayor Helmut Zilk when he opened a letter in his home in December 1993. Others have suffered injuries to their hands and face.
A pipe bomb left outside a Slovenian-language school in the southern city of Klagenfurt in August 1994 blew the hands off a police officer who was handling the device.
The shadowy BLA is believed to be a group which hankers after an ancient German-speaking zone, linking Bavaria with the Alps and Danube region.
